profile.summary: ESA-dna2vec is the DNA embedding model from the Embed-Search-Align (ESA) work, which treats read alignment as a search problem. A transformer encoder turns a DNA read or a reference genome fragment into a single vector, so that a read lands close to the fragment it came from. Reads are then aligned by searching a vector store of reference fragment embeddings and refining the best hits with Smith-Waterman scoring.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model, called the Reference-Free DNA Embedding (RDE) model in the paper, is a transformer encoder with 12 heads, 6 encoder layers, a vocabulary of 10,000 tokens and 1020-dimensional output vectors. It is trained self-supervised with a contrastive loss: a read sampled from a reference fragment is pulled towards that fragment's embedding and pushed away from a batch of random fragments. The card describes fragments of 800 to 2000 bases, reads of 150 to 500 bases, and 1 to 5% random base substitutions added to 40% of training reads. For alignment, the reference genome is cut into overlapping fragments, each fragment is embedded and stored in a vector database, and each read retrieves its top-K nearest fragments per chromosome before Smith-Waterman scoring picks the best location.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is on Hugging Face as roychowdhuryresearch/dna2vec; this page read revision 6e15acaa. It loads through transformers with custom model code from the repository (trust_remote_code=True), and the card adds a mean-pooling step over the last hidden state to get one vector per sequence. The paper says model checkpoints are also on OSF, and the training code is in a co-author's repository, KennethEnevoldsen/dna2vec, whose readme calls it DNA-ESA. The GUANinE benchmark lists the model as the contrastive dna2vec of Embed-Search-Align but the sources read do not say which copy it used. A result should name the Hugging Face revision and the pooling used.

strengths.text: Trained for sequence similarity rather than classification, so distances between read and fragment embeddings track where a read comes from. The authors report alignment recall close to Bowtie-2 on simulated reads.

quotes.text: RDE is 99% accurate when aligning 250-length reads onto a human reference genome of 3 gigabases (single-haploid)
is comparable to Bowtie-2 to within 1%

strengths.text: Small (55 million parameters), MIT licensed, ungated, and loads in a few lines through Hugging Face transformers.
strengths.source_locator: Hugging Face API. Model card: Installation; Usage

strengths.text: The authors report that the model, trained on human sequence, also embeds reads from other species such as Thermus aquaticus.

quotes.text: We show how the RDE model—trained on exemplars from the human genome—can effectively embed simulated reads from a very different species, Thermus Aquaticus.

limitations.text: Trained on samples covering only about 2% of the human genome; the authors list broader training data as future work.

quotes.text: our RDE models have been trained using samples that span only around 2% of the human genome

limitations.text: Built for short reads and fragments (150 to 2000 bases) with 1024 positions; it is not designed for long-range genomic context.

run_guide.summary: Install transformers and torch, load the dna2vec checkpoint from Hugging Face and print the shape of a mean-pooled embedding for one DNA sequence.
prerequisites: Python with pip. The sources do not state GPU or memory needs.
Network access to Hugging Face; the model loads with trust_remote_code=True.
Weights are MIT licensed and not gated.

steps.title: Embed a sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

def load_hf_model():
    hf_model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("roychowdhuryresearch/dna2vec", trust_remote_code=True)
    hf_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("roychowdhuryresearch/dna2vec", trust_remote_code=True)

    class AveragePooler(nn.Module):
        def forward(self, last_hidden, attention_mask):
            return (last_hidden * attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(1) / attention_mask.sum(-1).unsqueeze(-1)

    hf_model.pooler = AveragePooler()
    return hf_model, hf_tokenizer, hf_model.pooler

def get_embedding(dna_sequence):
    model, tokenizer, pooler = load_hf_model()
    tokenized_input = tokenizer(dna_sequence, return_tensors="pt", padding=True)
    with torch.no_grad():
        output = model(**tokenized_input)
    embedding = pooler(output.last_hidden_state, tokenized_input.attention_mask)
    return embedding.numpy()

dna_seq = "ATGCGTACGTAGCTAGCTAGC"
embedding = get_embedding(dna_seq)
print("Embedding shape:", embedding.shape)
PY

notes: The record name 'ESA-dna2vec' comes from GUANinE, which describes it only as 'the contrastive dna2vec of Embed-Search-Align'; it is unrelated to the older word2vec-style dna2vec (pnpnpn/dna2vec). The Hugging Face checkpoint is under the lab of the paper's senior author (Roychowdhury) and its card cites the paper, so it is treated as official. GitHub repository KennethEnevoldsen/dna2vec (a co-author) calls itself DNA-ESA code; it has no licence and is not linked from the paper, so only its readme was used, hashed and not stored. Code licence is taken from the Hugging Face card metadata, which covers the modeling_dna2vec.py file in that repository.
